candidates.bio: Rach is a Quebec rapper and former beatmaker from Laval-des-Rapides. He emerged through tracks such as Chief Keef, Sans refrain, FNG and collaborations with J.BO, JPS and Tizzo, building a catalogue rooted in Laval's francophone street-rap scene. His feature on JMB Drippy's 2021 single Palmarès is the RACH credit in the Northern Dial library.
Toronto group Raggadeath was a Canadian rap-metal and reggae-rock project whose mid-1990s recordings fused heavy guitars with dancehall rhythms and featured vocalists including Michie Mee.
Toronto-born, Calgary-raised singer-songwriter Raghav blends R&B, pop, reggae fusion and Indian pop in a crossover catalogue that found major audiences in Canada and the United Kingdom.
Montréal Haitian-Canadian hip-hop duo Rainmen is a pioneering Québec rap group whose catalogue dates to the late 1990s and remains rooted in the city's francophone scene.
Toronto singer-songwriter RALPH, born Raffaela Weyman, makes polished synth-pop, disco and smooth soul shaped by nostalgic influences and contemporary pop production.

Formed in Vancouver in the early 1990s, Rascalz became one of the most consequential groups in the development of Canadian hip-hop outside Toronto. Built around MCs Red1 and Misfit and DJ Kemo, with breakers Zebroc and Dedos part of the wider crew, the group treated MCing, DJing, graffiti and breaking as connected parts of hip-hop culture. They first recorded as Ragga Muffin Rascals before releasing Really Livin', then reached a much larger national audience with 1997's Cash Crop, a record that established the West Coast as a serious centre of Canadian rap rather than a regional afterthought.

Cash Crop won the 1998 JUNO for Best Rap Recording, but Rascalz refused the award because the rap category was presented during the non-televised portion of the ceremony. Their protest drew attention to the marginalization of Black music within Canada's biggest music awards, and the following year the rap award moved onto the televised broadcast. Rascalz then returned with "Northern Touch," produced by Kemo and featuring Checkmate, Kardinal Offishall, Thrust and Choclair. The cross-country posse cut became a landmark Canadian rap anthem, won the 1999 JUNO and was performed on the broadcast, giving the country's hip-hop community a rare national showcase at a moment when domestic rap still struggled for mainstream infrastructure.

The group followed with Global Warning in 1999 and Reloaded in the early 2000s, but Rascalz's lasting significance rests as much on what they changed around the music as on their catalogue. "Northern Touch" linked Vancouver and Toronto scenes into a shared national statement, while the JUNO protest challenged an industry practice that had kept rap out of prime view. Together, those moments made Rascalz a bridge between Canada's underground hip-hop networks and the more visible national ecosystem that followed, and established Vancouver as an essential part of that history.

Ray Robinson is a Canadian R&B singer-songwriter associated with Toronto's independent soul and urban music scene. Active since the 2000s, he has released projects including What It Is, Do You Hear Me and SUNray, with his work spanning contemporary R&B, soul and hip-hop collaborations.

Ray Smoove is a Toronto hip-hop artist associated with Ghetto Concept, Unit 7 and the 7Bills scene. His credits span classic Toronto recordings including Heat of the Night, Blades of Ice, No Love in the Streets and later Ghetto Concept projects. Northern Dial carries Ray Smoove as part of its archival Toronto hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto-born, Brampton-raised rapper and producer Raz Fresco is a Canadian hip-hop artist known for sample-heavy production, dense lyricism and his Bakers Club collective.
Scarborough-born singer-songwriter RealestK, born Rony Kordab, is a Canadian R&B artist known for melancholic, trap-inflected vocals and the breakout single WFM.
Vancouver MC Red-1 is a veteran of Canadian hip-hop and a founding member of the Rascalz, the influential West Coast group behind the landmark all-star single Northern Touch.
Rexdale group Redlife was a Canadian 1990s hip-hop act produced by DJ K-Note, known for hard-edged Toronto street rap and a Juno-nominated catalogue including Who's Talkin' Weight.
Toronto-born emcee, producer, singer, songwriter, engineer and DJ Rel McCoy, formerly Relic the Oddity, is a Canadian independent hip-hop artist now based in Spain.

Winnipeg singer-songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Remy Shand arrived with one of the most striking Canadian R&B debuts of the early 2000s. He developed The Way I Feel largely in his own home-studio environment, writing, arranging and producing the material himself while playing the instruments across the record. Motown and Universal released the album internationally in 2002, placing a young Canadian musician directly inside the neo-soul conversation then being shaped by artists such as D'Angelo, Maxwell and Jill Scott. Songs including "Take a Message," "Rocksteady" and the title track paired vintage soul vocabulary with unusually self-contained musicianship.

The Way I Feel reached No. 1 in Canada, was certified platinum domestically and gave Shand a rare U.S. crossover for a Canadian R&B artist of that period. At the 2003 Grammy Awards, the album and its songs earned four nominations: Best R&B Album, Best Male R&B Vocal Performance and Best R&B Song for "Take a Message," and Best Traditional R&B Vocal Performance for "Rocksteady." The record also won the 2003 JUNO Award for R&B/Soul Recording of the Year. That level of recognition made Shand's breakthrough notable not simply as a strong debut but as evidence that a self-produced Winnipeg soul record could compete inside the North American R&B industry.

Shand largely withdrew from the conventional major-label spotlight after that first album, making his catalogue unusually compact for an artist whose debut generated so much attention. He resurfaced independently during the 2010s with new and archival material, while Universal and Motown marked The Way I Feel's 20th anniversary with expanded reissues. The album's durability has become part of his legacy: one concentrated body of work established Shand as a distinctive Canadian neo-soul figure and remains a useful snapshot of the country's R&B ambitions immediately before Toronto became an internationally recognized centre for the genre.

Renny Holladae is a Toronto hip-hop producer and artist associated with the city's independent rap community. His production credits include work with Scarborough artist KinSmuv and collaborations within Toronto's long-running underground scene, including artists connected to Motive Music. Northern Dial carries Renny Holladae as part of its Toronto hip-hop and production catalogue.

Toronto's Rheostatics became one of Canada's most idiosyncratic and influential art-rock bands by treating the country itself as material for experimentation. Formed in Etobicoke and active through a changing lineup centred on songwriters Dave Bidini, Martin Tielli and Tim Vesely, the group developed a deliberately unstable mix of punk, folk, progressive rock, pop and improvisation. The early independent years led to Melville in 1991 and Whale Music in 1992, two records that became enduring critical touchstones even though the band rarely operated like a conventional commercial-rock act. Songs such as "Horses," "Record Body Count" and "Claire" showed how their work could be funny, unruly, melodic and deeply rooted in Canadian places and stories at the same time.

That relationship with Canadian culture became even more explicit in the mid-1990s. Rheostatics wrote music for the film Whale Music and created Music Inspired by the Group of Seven, a commissioned work associated with the National Gallery of Canada that translated the painters' landscapes into an expansive instrumental suite. Albums including Introducing Happiness and The Blue Hysteria pushed the band's restless writing further, while touring with The Tragically Hip placed their eccentric catalogue in front of much larger audiences. Their commercial peak was modest compared with many contemporaries, but Melville and Whale Music repeatedly appeared near the top of Canadian best-album polls, reflecting the unusual depth of the band's reputation among musicians, critics and committed listeners.

Rheostatics initially ended their run with a 2007 farewell at Massey Hall, then gradually reunited and returned to recording. Here Come the Wolves arrived in 2019, and the 2025 project The Great Lakes Suite extended the band's long-standing practice of using Canadian geography, history and collaboration as creative structure. That longevity helps explain why Rheostatics matter: rather than exporting a simplified idea of Canadian rock, they built a body of work whose oddness, humour, regional detail and willingness to change form made Canadian identity itself feel open-ended.
Brampton singer-songwriter Rhyan Douglas is a Canadian artist whose atmospheric music blends contemporary R&B, folk and soul around guitar, ethereal production and a flexible falsetto.
Rhye is the alternative-R&B project led by Toronto-born Canadian singer and producer Mike Milosh, known for intimate vocals, minimal arrangements and atmospheric soul.

Halifax singer-songwriter Ria Mae developed through Atlantic Canada's independent music circuit before moving decisively toward pop. Her early album Under Your Skin earned East Coast recognition and established her as a songwriter first, but the major national breakthrough came after she began working with Halifax rapper and producer Classified. Their collaboration "Clothes Off" became a platinum Canadian hit and earned a JUNO nomination for Single of the Year, giving Mae the platform for a much larger radio audience.

Her 2016 major-label album sharpened that pop direction with "Clothes Off" and the gold-certified "Ooh Love." The My Love EP followed, while "Bend" became another platinum single and reached the upper tier of Canadian radio. Mae toured with artists including Tegan and Sara, Dido and Scott Helman, and her catalogue increasingly balanced direct pop hooks with the personal perspective that had shaped her earlier singer-songwriter work. Songs such as "Girlfriend" also made queer identity more explicit within that mainstream-pop setting.

By the mid-2020s, Mae had accumulated three JUNO nominations, multiple East Coast Music Awards and tens of millions of streams while remaining closely tied to Halifax's collaborative music culture. Her 2025 album Two and 2026 Classified collaboration "In the Stars" extended a career that has consistently moved between Atlantic Canadian roots and national pop radio. Mae matters as one of the artists who helped demonstrate that polished contemporary pop could emerge from Halifax without severing its connection to the city's independent songwriting community.
Toronto producer, rapper, songwriter and director Rich Kidd is a versatile Canadian hip-hop figure known for his own mixtapes and production for artists including Drake, k-os and Nelly Furtado.

Richie Payso is a Toronto-area rapper associated with the G7 Records camp founded by Ghetto Concept's Kwajo Cinqo. His early catalogue includes the Ghetto Celeb project and collaborations with labelmates including LP Da Original, placing him within the independent Toronto hip-hop scene of the early 2010s.

Richie Sosa is a Canadian rapper from Toronto's east end whose career helped shape the city's pre-breakthrough mixtape era. Born Omar West Forbes and raised in East Scarborough, he built a prolific independent catalogue, wrote for producer Boi-1da and collaborated with Drake on Easy to Please from the 2007 mixtape Comeback Season.
Montréal DJ, rapper and songwriter Ricky J is a Canadian recording artist known for early-2000s pop-rap hits including No Means No and later the gold-certified Whatta Night.

Toronto singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer River Tiber, born Tommy Paxton-Beesley, makes textured alternative R&B and has contributed to music by artists including Drake, Travis Scott and BADBADNOTGOOD.

Ro Dolla is a Toronto artist, producer and creative known for his work with The Circle and the R&B and hip-hop group Big Black Lincoln. A longtime figure in Toronto music, he has collaborated with artists including Saukrates and Choclair while extending his creative work beyond recording. Northern Dial carries Ro Dolla as part of its Toronto hip-hop and R&B history catalogue.

Robb Klarke is a Milton, Ontario-based multidisciplinary artist and musician connected to Canadian hip-hop. His work includes visual and animation projects for Toronto rap artists as well as a featured performance with Saukrates and Dankery Harv on My Luv from Saukrates' Amani deluxe EP. Northern Dial carries Robb Klarke as part of its Greater Toronto Area hip-hop and multidisciplinary arts catalogue.
Toronto rapper Robin Banks, born Liban Randall, is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose melodic street rap and collaborations with Pressa helped define the city's mid-2010s Jane-Finch sound.
Toronto-raised singer Rochelle Jordan blends futuristic R&B with house, garage, electronic pop and hip-hop influences in a sleek, club-informed catalogue.
Toronto rapper Rochester is a Canadian hip-hop artist and lyricist whose catalogue includes collaborations with producers such as Boi-1da and longtime work across the city's independent scene.

Rolo is a Toronto underground hip-hop artist represented on the 1998 local compilation Invading the Mega City. The release credits Rolo with King David on 'Warriors Come Thru,' while Northern Dial also carries Rolo's 'In T.O.' The compilation documents Toronto-based independent rap artists from the era.
Toronto-born Canadian musician Romy Lightman is an experimental singer-songwriter and visual artist known for Tasseomancy, Lightman & Lightman and Lightman Jarvis Ecstatic Band.
Toronto rapper Roney, born Tyrone Smith, is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose gritty street rap, melodic flows and long-running Don't Sleep mixtape series built a large local following.

New Westminster-born Rosette Sharma, known professionally as Rosette, is a Canadian pop and dance singer-songwriter. Her career spans the Canadian edition of Popstars, independent releases and the 2012 dance hit Amnesia with Ian Carey, Timbaland and Brasco, which was certified Gold in Canada.

rossy is a Toronto-based independent artist whose catalogue blends rap, alternative rock and melodic songwriting. His artist profile explicitly lists Toronto and includes tracks such as young addicts that reflect his crossover sound. Northern Dial carries rossy as part of its contemporary Toronto independent music catalogue.
Brampton-born singer, rapper and songwriter Roy Woods blends R&B, hip-hop and trap and became one of the early Canadian artists signed to Drake's OVO Sound label.

Calgary R&B and soul singer-songwriter Ruben Young has built an independent Canadian catalogue around smooth vocals, contemporary soul and collaborations with artists and producers across hip-hop and R&B.
Shelburne, Ontario singer-songwriter Ruby Waters mixes raw, bluesy alternative rock with folk and pop, pairing commanding vocals with introspective writing.

Montréal-raised Canadian-American singer-songwriter and composer Rufus Wainwright is known for ornate art-pop, piano-driven songwriting, theatrical performances and work in opera and classical composition.

Runway the Catwalker is an Ajax, Ontario artist, songwriter and producer based in Toronto whose genre-bending work moves through rap, punk, indie and alternative music. Alongside his own releases, he has built an international songwriting and production résumé that includes work connected to Doja Cat, A$AP Rocky, Yxng Bane and D-Block Europe.
Toronto-born comedian, actor and producer Russell Peters is a Canadian recording artist whose platinum-selling stand-up albums document a career built around multicultural observational comedy.
Edmonton-born singer-songwriter Ruth B. makes piano-led alternative pop and R&B, rising from short-form social media performances into a globally streamed Canadian songwriting career.
Edmonton singer-songwriter Ruth B. is a Canadian pop artist whose career grew from short-form social media performances into the multi-platinum breakout single Lost Boy and a Juno Award.

Ryael is the stage name of East Toronto-born R&B singer Isrrael, a Canadian artist whose music blends contemporary soul, R&B and melodic pop. Raised in a musical family, he has built an independent catalogue including Lover's Prayer, Midnight Confession and Changes while performing across Toronto's live R&B circuit.
Deseronto, Ontario singer-songwriter and pianist Ryland James is a Canadian pop and soul vocalist whose powerful delivery draws on gospel roots and contemporary songwriting.
Toronto singer and songwriter SadBoi, formerly known as Ebhoni, is a Canadian alternative-R&B artist whose music draws on dancehall, reggae, soca and contemporary pop.
Abu Dhabi-born, Toronto-rooted singer, rapper and songwriter SAFE makes atmospheric contemporary R&B that blends tender balladry with trap, dancehall and Afrobeats influences.
Toronto-born singer, songwriter and dancer Sage Harris is a Canadian R&B artist whose performance-driven work combines contemporary soul, pop and choreography.
Vancouver indie-rock band Said the Whale combines melodic guitar pop, indie folk and distinctly West Coast songwriting in a long-running Canadian catalogue.

Montreal-raised singer-songwriter Sajaa. is an R&B and soul artist whose smoky jazz-inflected vocals and confessional writing draw on influences including Lauryn Hill, D'Angelo, Joss Stone and Amy Winehouse. Her independent catalogue includes the EPs Blurred Minds & Perspectives and Vivid Dreams & Intuitions.

Salia Joseph is a Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and Snuneymuxw singer, cultural worker and language advocate from British Columbia. Alongside her work in Indigenous arts and language revitalization, she has contributed vocals to Snotty Nose Rez Kids records including M.I.N.A.Y., Broke Boy Ambitions and H.O.W. from The Average Savage.
